channel.title: Daily World Bulletin
channel.description: Clear, sourced news across India and the world

item.title: CJI Surya Kant disapproves BCI action against NALSAR students
item.description: Chief Justice Surya Kant has strongly criticized the Bar Council of India for its disciplinary actions against NALSAR University students. The students had previously staged a protest regarding judicial matters. Emphasizing that peaceful dissent is a fundamental right, the Chief Justice questioned the authority of the Bar Council to intervene in matters concerning students and the judiciary. He remarked that any concerns should remain strictly between the students and himself, leading to widespread calls for a reconsideration of the official regulatory measures.

item.title: Six dead in unprecedented Japan rainstorm
item.description: Severe downpours described as unprecedented have resulted in six deaths across Japan. The heavy storm disrupted daily life by cutting power supplies to over twenty thousand households. Additionally, transport operations were significantly affected, leaving approximately seven thousand travellers stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport. Authorities are responding to the emergency caused by the extreme weather conditions. Further details regarding the total extent of the damage remain limited as recovery efforts continue.

item.title: Readers share tips on cancelling unwanted subscriptions and getting refunds
item.description: Following government announcements regarding a crackdown on subscription traps, readers have shared their experiences of escaping unwanted recurring payment plans. Individuals discussed how they managed to cancel services they no longer required and successfully secured financial refunds. These insights highlight common pitfalls associated with automatic renewals and offer practical guidance for consumers looking to navigate and avoid hidden subscription charges effectively.

item.title: Tanzid Hasan hits historic ton to put Bangladesh in command against Australia
item.description: During the Darwin Test, Tanzid Hasan Tamim justified his selection by scoring a remarkable maiden century, putting Bangladesh in a commanding position on Day 2. His performance helped Bangladesh secure an 88-run lead against Australia, whose bowlers struggled on a difficult day. Meanwhile, former captain Ricky Ponting criticised Australian selectors following the team's poor showing on the field. Further details regarding the ongoing match remain limited as proceedings continue.

item.title: Awarapan 2 leads Batwara 1947 at Independence Day box office
item.description: The Independence Day box office clash features Emraan Hashmi's thriller 'Awarapan 2' taking the lead against Sunny Deol's partition drama 'Batwara 1947'. While 'Awarapan 2' has raced ahead in ticket sales, reviews indicate that the Emraan Hashmi starrer faces script limitations and criticism over relying on nostalgia. Meanwhile, 'Batwara 1947' has received positive reviews from audiences and critics alike, setting up an interesting theatrical competition between the two major releases during the holiday period.

item.description: A recent study published by EMJ highlights that vitamin D deficiency is prevalent among a significant majority of children. The research emphasizes the widespread nature of this health concern in the pediatric population. Experts suggest that further investigation is needed to understand the implications of these findings on child health. item.title: Indian solar mission reveals new clues about Sun's corona
item.description: India's solar mission has shared new findings that help address long-standing questions regarding the Sun. Researchers are examining why the solar corona is significantly hotter than the surface and how it sustains such extreme temperatures. These insights from the spacecraft contribute to our understanding of stellar mechanics and solar physics, offering potential answers to mysteries that have puzzled astronomers for years. Further analysis of the mission data is expected to reveal more details about solar activity.

item.description: Japanese automobile and motorcycle manufacturers are supporting India's ongoing efforts to reduce fossil fuel consumption. This collaboration highlights the growing alignment between international automotive companies and national environmental goals in the region. item.title: Delhi weather: IMD predicts cloudy skies, light rain
item.description: Ahead of Independence Day, the national capital is expected to experience generally cloudy skies accompanied by light rain, according to the latest weather forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department. These climatic conditions are likely to offer pleasant weather conditions for citizens participating in the national celebrations. Authorities and commuters have been advised to stay updated on localized forecasts as minor showers may influence daily movement across the city during this festive period.

item.title: Air India A320 faced rare flight control loss on Phuket route, Airbus report shows
item.description: An initial Airbus analysis indicates that an Air India A320 aircraft briefly lost key flight controls during a Phuket-Delhi flight, leading to a sudden altitude drop. Pilots reportedly struggled to manage the rare malfunction. Airbus has shared its initial report with the airline and requested specific maintenance records. Meanwhile, this incident follows separate reports regarding an Air India CEO warning issued after a pilot drug test controversy. Further details regarding the exact technical failure and subsequent safety measures remain limited.

item.description: According to the mayor of Qusra, Israeli forces have instructed Palestinian families to leave their residences in a village where Israeli settlers besieged local houses. The mayor stated that troops are also using some of these vacated properties as military barracks. Further details regarding the unfolding situation and the exact number of affected residents are currently limited based on the available reports from the area.

item.title: South Korean stock market volatility causes heavy investor losses
item.description: Traders in South Korea are facing severe financial setbacks following a sudden and brutal correction in the local stock market. Several investors have reported substantial losses within a very short span, with one individual losing thousands of dollars in just a month. This sharp downturn highlights the unpredictable nature and wild swings currently affecting the region's financial markets, leaving many market participants struggling to cope with the aftermath of the steep market drop.

item.title: Manpreet Singh eyes World Cup title to end India's wait
item.description: Senior Indian hockey player Manpreet Singh has indicated that the upcoming tournament could potentially be his final World Cup appearance. As the team prepares for the prestigious event, players and coaches are focusing on managing tournament pressure, trusting their rigorous preparations, and refining key areas like defence and set-pieces. With inputs from former greats and dedicated mental conditioning through visualisation, the squad remains determined to lift the trophy and end the country's long-standing wait for the title, according to reports.

item.title: Batwara 1947 Sells 20,000 Tickets in Advance Booking
item.description: Rajkumar Santoshi directed film Batwara 1947, starring Sunny Deol and Shabana Azmi, has recorded an advance booking of 20,000 tickets across major national chains. Early social media reviews praise Sunny Deol's performance and describe the movie as a mass entertainer, while Shabana Azmi's acting has been appreciated by audiences. The film's overall box office success and final fate now depend entirely on positive audience reception during its theatrical run. Detailed box office figures remain limited as reviews continue to emerge.

item.title: New study shows mosquito bites could help boost immunity against malaria
item.description: Recent scientific research explores an innovative approach to combat malaria by targeting the parasite inside the insect while allowing mosquitoes to survive. Instead of solely preventing bites, this method investigates whether controlled exposure through mosquito bites might help transform them into natural immune boosters. Institutes such as the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research and HHMI are involved in studying this potential new front in disease eradication. However, further details regarding the clinical application and widespread effectiveness of this method remain limited.

item.title: Maharashtra Cop's Quick Response Saves Sukhbir Badal
item.description: A prompt reaction by a Maharashtra police officer prevented a major incident during an attack on Shiromani Akali Dal leader Sukhbir Badal in Nanded. Following the incident, Mr. Badal stated he was unafraid. Medical professionals confirmed that the SAD chief underwent a surgery lasting ninety minutes and is currently in stable condition. Meanwhile, leaders including Harsimrat Kaur Badal expressed gratitude for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's support, as political discussions regarding the attack and related events continue across news platforms.

item.title: US Report Alleges Dozens of Nations Helped China Dodge Tariffs
item.description: A recent United States report claims that numerous countries assisted China in circumventing higher import duties imposed during the Trump administration. According to the findings, Chinese goods were routed through nations with lower tariff rates to avoid the steeper levies. Details regarding the specific countries involved and the full scope of the report remain limited based on the initial information provided.

item.title: Tata Steel sells Jamshedpur FC stake to Churchill Brothers
item.description: Tata Steel has transferred its complete ownership in Jamshedpur FC to Churchill Brothers for a nominal amount of one hundred rupees. The transaction also includes the transfer of the Indian Super League license. Meanwhile, discussions regarding broadcast partners and the upcoming season schedule continue among clubs ahead of the anticipated October start for the league.

item.title: Nicole Kidman reveals warning against marrying Tom Cruise
item.description: Actor Nicole Kidman has disclosed that she was advised against marrying Tom Cruise, with people cautioning her that the decision could negatively impact her professional career. In recent interviews, Kidman reflected on her past marriage and the choices she made during that period. The actor discussed how her life and career trajectory were influenced by her high-profile relationship and subsequent divorce, offering insights into the challenges she faced in the film industry at the time.

item.title: Indian Scientists Develop AI Tool to Detect Hidden Cancer Cells
item.description: Indian researchers have created a new artificial intelligence tool utilizing deep learning to identify hidden cancer cells, surpassing existing detection methods. Backed by the Department of Science and Technology, this technology successfully detects hidden cancer stem cells linked to tumor recurrence and maps cells capable of causing later metastases. Experts note this advancement unlocks valuable biological insights from current data, paving the way forward for precision medicine and more targeted cancer treatment strategies.

item.title: NASA shares view of August 2026 solar eclipse
item.description: Details are limited as NASA highlighted a celestial event where the Moon moved between the Sun and Earth. This alignment created a striking total solar eclipse that will be visible from Spain in August 2026. The phenomenon offers scientists and observers a remarkable opportunity to witness the rare cosmic alignment.

item.title: Mumbai weather: Moderate rain likely today, IMD issues yellow alert for Thane
item.description: The weather department has forecast moderate rainfall for Mumbai today. Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for the neighbouring district of Thane. Residents are advised to stay updated on local weather conditions as precipitation is expected to continue. Official sources have shared timely advisories to help the public plan their daily commutes and activities accordingly.

item.title: Census 2027 to feature 40 questions including caste and vaccination details
item.description: The central government has notified the questionnaire for the household schedule of Census 2027, featuring forty questions. The upcoming census will gather information on various subjects, including caste details, COVID-19 vaccination status, and identification proofs such as Aadhaar. item.title: Ryanair Window Smashed After Engine Blade Broke, Report Says
item.description: A preliminary report released by US investigators reveals that an engine fan blade broke during a flight from Greece to Germany last month, causing engine parts to smash a window. According to the report, a passenger's head was partially sucked out through the damaged window during the incident. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the exact sequence of events that led to the dangerous structural failure. Official details regarding the condition of the passenger and further safety recommendations from the aviation authorities are currently limited.

item.title: Barcelona and PSG agree €50 million transfer fee for Ferran Torres
item.description: Reports indicate that FC Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain have reached an agreement for the transfer of forward Ferran Torres for a reported fee of €50 million. This potential departure from the Spanish club could pave the way for Barcelona to pursue a deal for another World Cup-winning player. Media sources suggest the structure of the sale has been arranged to bypass a €10 million payment clause involving Manchester City. Further official details regarding the finalization of the transfer remain limited at this stage.

item.title: Ergonomic tools for young professionals with neck and back pain
item.description: Occupational therapist Bharati Jajoo has shared five ergonomic tools to help young professionals manage neck and back pain. With many individuals spending long hours working at desks, musculoskeletal discomfort has become increasingly common among the younger workforce. Proper workplace ergonomics can significantly reduce physical strain and improve overall posture. Incorporating these supportive tools into daily routines may help prevent chronic issues and promote better spinal health in office environments.

item.title: NASA Repaints 737 Aircraft for Reduced Gravity Testing
item.description: NASA's 737 aircraft received a new paint job in Oklahoma as part of ongoing modifications to prepare it as a reduced gravity test vehicle. NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, acquired the plane from the United States Air Force in June. The modified aircraft is scheduled to conduct lunar-gravity parabolic flights to validate equipment and procedures for future space missions. Further details regarding the testing schedule and specific mission parameters remain limited at this stage.

item.title: Supreme Court Quashes Defamation Case Against Rahul Gandhi
item.description: The Supreme Court has quashed a criminal defamation complaint and summons issued against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. The legal action originated from his remarks regarding Veer Savarkar, wherein he termed him a British collaborator. The top court set aside the Lucknow court order, providing relief to the politician. Legal reports confirm the cancellation of the proceedings tied to the controversial comments. Details regarding the specific observations made by the bench are limited at present.

item.title: US Navy sailors face severe hardships aboard deployed aircraft carrier
item.description: Thousands of crew members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly endured challenging conditions during a deployment lasting over 250 days. Reports indicate that the sailors faced issues such as food shortages and broken plumbing facilities while at sea. The situation has raised significant concerns, with some individuals even considering jumping overboard due to the prolonged and difficult circumstances. Further official details regarding the ship's current operational status and mitigation measures remain limited at this time.

item.title: VVS Laxman likely to be named BCCI Director of Cricket
item.description: Reports indicate that VVS Laxman is set to take over as the BCCI Director of Cricket. This development comes amidst discussions regarding major organizational changes following recent team performances, including the series against England. Media reports highlight potential shifts in roles within the Indian cricket setup, impacting key figures like Gautam Gambhir and Ajit Agarkar. Further official announcements are awaited to confirm the exact nature of these appointments and the future roadmap for Indian cricket administration under the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

item.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Makes Box Office History in North America
item.description: The Tom Holland starrer 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' has achieved a significant box office milestone in North America, becoming the fastest film to cross the $700 million mark and securing a place in the all-time top six movies. Meanwhile, the film continues its strong theatrical run in India, nearing substantial gross collections by the end of its second week and preparing to compete with upcoming domestic releases.

item.title: Ebola tracing improves in DR Congo, but virus continues to spread
item.description: Efforts to trace Ebola contacts have improved in the Democratic Republic of Congo, yet the ongoing outbreak remains ahead of containment measures. According to the WHO chief, the epidemic is on course to become the deadliest in the region's history. The fast-moving virus has now affected a sixth province, with officials confirming a new fatality. Experts note that the outbreak stems from a new animal transmission event, posing continuous challenges for health workers trying to control the spread.

item.title: West Virginia Engineer Finds Inspiring Path to NASA Career
item.description: Fletcher Newell grew up in Grafton, West Virginia, developing an early fascination with science fiction and space. His passion for exploration intensified in 2013 during a fourth-grade school field trip to a nearby NASA facility, specifically NASA’s Katherine Johnson Independent Verification and Validation facility. This pivotal early experience eventually guided him toward pursuing a professional career in engineering and space science within his home state, connecting his childhood dreams with practical contributions to ongoing space missions.

item.title: PM Modi and leaders observe Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
item.description: On Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the historical event tore apart several lives, recalling the immense pain and suffering endured by the people. Political leaders across the nation paid tributes to those affected, remembering the courage and resilience shown during the crisis. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma noted that the scars of the partition will never be forgotten, while other leaders emphasized honouring the lives lost and impacted by the tragedy, ensuring that the historical lessons remain alive in the national memory.

item.title: Stolen Matisse artworks recovered by police in Brazil
item.description: Brazilian police have recovered eight stolen artworks by the renowned French artist Henri Matisse following an investigation. Authorities arrested a man after locating the valuable pieces inside a residential home situated in the greater São Paulo area. Details regarding the exact circumstances of the recovery and the condition of the artworks are currently limited. The police action marks a significant development in tracking down the missing cultural items.

item.title: India prepares for Galle Test amid pitch intrigue and crosswinds
item.description: The Indian cricket team has stepped up training sessions in Galle ahead of their upcoming first Test match against Sri Lanka. While questions surround the nature of the pitch and challenging local crosswinds have added tactical intrigue to the fixture, reports indicate that the visiting squad is likely to choose a conventional and cautious path for the opening encounter. Meanwhile, players including KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant were spotted unwinding during the tour preparations, as the team puts in rigorous practice hours before the series begins.

item.description: Details are limited regarding singer Sunidhi Chauhan's Mumbai residence, which features contemporary design elements. item.title: Tobacco quit services scarce in low and middle income nations
item.description: Experts report that health systems in developing nations are failing smokers due to a lack of adequate support. Tobacco cessation services remain extremely scarce across low-and middle-income countries. Meanwhile, health professionals suggest that a straightforward three-step method could assist individuals in quitting tobacco consumption. While quitting smoking poses significant challenges in poorer countries, experts emphasize the urgent need for improved cessation resources and stronger health systems to help individuals overcome nicotine addiction.

item.title: Seven Dead and Three Trapped After Water Floods Tunnel in Uttarakhand's Chamoli
item.description: Seven workers died and three remain trapped following a water flooding incident inside a tunnel in Chamoli, Uttarakhand. Fourteen others sustained injuries in the disaster. Rescue teams have launched operations, including underwater efforts, to locate and save the missing individuals. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami visited the accident site to monitor rescue work and met with injured workers receiving treatment. The state government announced an ex-gratia financial assistance of four lakh rupees for the families of each deceased worker, as relief and rescue efforts continue at the location.

item.title: Romania shuts sole nuclear plant due to Danube River heat
item.description: Romania has closed its only nuclear facility, the Cernavodă plant, because a significant drop in the water level of the Danube River was caused by intense heat. The plant is responsible for generating twenty percent of the nation's electricity supply. Authorities do not anticipate restarting operations at the facility within the next ten days. Further details regarding the long-term impact on power generation remain limited at this time.

item.title: Harbhajan Singh reveals masterplan to stop Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
item.description: Former Indian cricketer Harbhajan Singh has shared his perspective on how to counter young cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, suggesting that attacking him is the only way to survive. Meanwhile, other former players including Matthew Hayden and Brett Lee have also praised the young talent, with Lee noting that his actual age remains a major talking point in the cricketing world. Expert analyses highlight the growing attention Sooryavanshi is attracting from cricket legends due to his exceptional abilities on the field.

item.title: Gujarat reports 27 deaths and 41 confirmed cases in Chandipura virus outbreak
item.description: The Gujarat government has reported that the Chandipura virus outbreak has claimed 27 lives in the state, with a total of 41 confirmed cases recorded. Multiple reports indicate that numerous children have been affected by the viral return over a span of several weeks. Experts are currently examining the situation regarding how the infection spreads, while health advisories continue to highlight symptoms, causes, treatment, and prevention methods to manage the ongoing public health concern.

item.title: Supreme Court Stays Madras HC Order on Compassionate Jobs
item.description: The Supreme Court has stayed a judgment by the Madras High Court that had previously quashed compassionate appointments for families affected by the Karur tragedy. During the proceedings, the apex court questioned whether the government should provide employment to the victims' kin, offering significant relief regarding the job provisions. Legal reports highlighted that the decision came after various petitions were reviewed, pausing the earlier high court ruling that had struck down these employment measures.

item.title: BJP Slams Rahul Gandhi Over Mock Hug Jibe At PM Modi
item.description: The Bharatiya Janata Party has strongly criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi following his recent remarks concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Several party leaders expressed strong disapproval, accusing the opposition leader of crossing lines of decency regarding foreign policy discussions. In response to the comments, BJP leader Nishikant Dubey referenced historical photographs to counter the remarks. The ongoing war of words has sparked a major political uproar across various media platforms, with the ruling party demanding maturity from the senior opposition figure.

item.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy takes voter list deletions seriously
item.description: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has expressed serious concern over the deletion of lakhs of voters during the SIR exercise, stating that a vote is more valuable than gold. Hyderabad authorities are set to issue notices to nearly 5.82 lakh unmapped voters. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister emphasized that communities like Hindus and Muslims are regarded as two eyes, and the state government is making continuous efforts to ensure equal benefits for Muslim citizens.

item.title: Rs 6,000 Crore Drug Case Kingpin Extradited From UAE
item.description: Fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya has been brought to India from Dubai in connection with a major multi-crore drug case. Home Minister Amit Shah highlighted the government's strict approach toward dismantling narcotics networks following the extradition. Basoya, described as a key cartel boss, was wanted in connection with a massive drug bust involving cocaine. Law enforcement agencies executed the transfer from the United Arab Emirates, marking a significant development in the high-profile investigation.

item.title: UNSC Report Links Al-Qaida Offshoot AQIS to 2025 Red Fort Blast
item.description: A recent United Nations Security Council report has officially attributed the November 2025 car bomb explosion near the Red Fort in Delhi to AQIS, an offshoot of Al-Qaida. The terrorist attack resulted in multiple casualties, with reports noting between 11 and 15 fatalities. The sanctions monitoring report confirms the direct involvement of the militant group in orchestrating the blast. Authorities continue to review the findings as international security bodies monitor extremist activities in the region.
